content.content: deccy stores the decision graph in a jj repository: one jj change owns one node, and jj versions the tree. deccy also keeps its undo journal — the before and after content of the paths a recording touched — as untracked state under `.deccy/`, never as graph state.
content.rationale: jj already gives history, rebase and undo over the tree the graph lives in, so the graph's history is real, inspectable VCS history instead of a bespoke store. The journal is the one thing jj's op log cannot supply for a recording: the before and after content of the owned paths, kept untracked beside the markers so it never enters the graph's own history. jj specifically — rather than any versioned store — is selected because change-based identity and built-in undo are what the node operations need: stable ids come free with change ids, and undo comes free with the op log.
